sub_questions.question: Is there a way to test what a knowledge base will retrieve before connecting it to a live app?

claims.claim: Yes, retrieval can be tested before plugging the knowledge base into a live app.
claims.guide_evidence: Before publishing an app that uses a dataset, the Hit Testing / retrieval-test panel on the dataset page lets a builder type a sample query

claims.claim: The Hit Testing panel is found on the dataset's page.
claims.guide_evidence: the Hit Testing / retrieval-test panel on the dataset page

claims.claim: You enter a sample query and see exactly which chunks would be retrieved, along with their similarity scores.
claims.guide_evidence: type a sample query and see exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores

claims.claim: This works without running the app.
claims.guide_evidence: without needing to run the full app

claims.claim: It is a useful way to check chunking and indexing before connecting the dataset to a retrieval node.
claims.guide_evidence: lets a builder type a sample query and see exactly which chunks would be retrieved

evaluation.rationale: The answer sends the customer to the Hit Testing panel on the dataset page. It also correctly says the panel shows which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores, without running the app. Every claim matches the guide, and the last sentence follows directly from what the guide says the panel does. The guide fully answers the question, so no escalation was needed, and the answer is safe to send as written.
